ambiguities_or_notes: Every source block (28) has a matching target block, with page markers, numbering, quotation structure, and italics preserved.

Website Circle of Reading paragraphs served as the first draft; each was re-read against the Russian and revised where it drifted (omissions, additions, generic he/his, terminology, attribution form); blocks 10 had no website counterpart and were translated fresh.

«Спор» (spor) is 'dispute' throughout and «доводы» (dovody) 'arguments'; Kant's «рассудок» (rassudok) is 'intellect'. «Пэн» (Pen) is given as 'Penn.', since the passage is William Penn's maxim from Some Fruits of Solitude, and the website draft's 'Pen' is dropped; the Carlyle attribution and the unattributed proverb «Кроткий ответ удаляет злобу» (krotkiy otvet udalyaet zlobu, 'a meek answer drives away malice') are translated from the Russian as printed.

Source observation: [10] The attribution «*Карлейл.*» stands outside the quotation markup (no «>») after an italic, unquoted line of the kind Tolstoy uses for his own thoughts, and the name is spelled «Карлейл» rather than the usual «Карлейль» (as in the 5 February file); reproduced as printed (unquoted).
Source observation: [26] The attribution «*Джон Рёскин*» (Dzhon Ryoskin, 'John Ruskin') lacks a final period, as in the 9 February file; probably a transcription slip. English mirrors it.
